doc.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Bethlehem albums and the Teddy Charles string album
summary: His Bethlehem albums and a string quartet album written by Teddy Charles, with Roy Haynes arriving at the last minute.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yeah. I don’t think he’s around anymore. So anyhow, so my friend brought it to Charlie Mingus, he liked it and he put it out. And so that started something. I think that was before I had, then I don’t remember what happened but I got four albums out on Bethlehem. I don’t know if you know anything about those?

I had one big band album, with a lot of the New York people. One of the things I had was do you remember a fellow Teddy Cohen? Vibe player? In fact I worked up in Syracuse with him with Pepper Adams, you know he had a group up there. Well anyhow he wrote, Hall Overton, who wrote the thing for Monk. I was studying with him for a little while, and he was too busy because I wanted him to write some music, so he asked Teddy Charles, Teddy Cohen, he changed his name, to write this string quartet album. So I had a string quartet album at that time I guess in the 50s, and I had Jimmy Raney and Art Farmer’s brother, and some of the Metropolitan Opera string people. It was really good and very modern. This guy I guess studied with Hall and had some things that sounded like Bartok at the time, with the strings and I played clarinet and flute on it. And I was going to mention a few things about it — oh yeah, and anyhow a half hour before the date, a drummer said, “I’m sending someone else down because I can’t make it but he’s good,” and guess who it was?
Oh. I guess he’s pretty good.

So he called me up a half hour before the date. And he sent in one of Lennie Tristano’s guys, Harold Barnowski, but I just wanted Roy. That might have made the whole difference with the thing. And anyhow, that’s the story with that thing. So I had one big band, then a quartet album with Bob Dorough and some other people and I got about four or five albums on Bethlehem, some arranged things at the time.
